user.title: Choose a country
user.description: Step {step}. Only countries whose tariffs the open store holds are listed.

data_description.country: The country whose suppliers you want to choose from.

plan.title: Choose a supplier and plan
plan.description: Step {step}. Plans with prices in force today. A third step follows only if the plan's prices differ by area. {country_note}

data_description.tariff: Your electricity supplier and the plan you are on. Only plans with prices in force today are listed. Choose your supplier and plan, or choose Type in my own rates at the top of the list. Type to search the list.

area.title: Choose an area
area.description: Step {step}. {plan} has different prices in different areas.

data_description.area: Pick the area of your supply. It is usually in the name of your distribution network or on your bill.

manual.title: Your own rates
manual.description: Prices as they appear on your bill. Timed rates, such as a night rate, are added next.

data.name: Name
data.bill_start_day: Day of the month a bill starts

data_description.name: A name for the tariff, shown as the integration's title.
data_description.currency: The three-letter currency code, such as EUR or GBP.
data_description.base_rate_name: The name shown for the rate that applies when no timed rate does.
data_description.base_rate: The price of one kWh at the main rate, as it appears on your bill. For example 0.30.
data_description.export_rate: What you are paid for one kWh exported. Leave at 0 if you are paid nothing.
data_description.standing_charge: The fixed charge for each day, before VAT unless you say prices include it.
data_description.levy: A fixed charge for each month, such as a public service levy. Leave at 0 if there is none.
data_description.discount_rate: A percentage taken off the energy charge, such as a prompt payment discount.
data_description.vat_rate: The VAT rate in percent. Leave at 0 if your prices already include it.
data_description.vat_included: Turn on when the rates above are the prices you pay, with VAT in them.
data_description.bill_start_day: The day of the month your supplier's bill period starts, 1 to 28.

manual_more.title: Timed rates
manual_more.description: Add a rate that applies at certain hours, such as a night rate. Where rates overlap, the cheapest applies.

data_description.name: A name for this timed rate, such as Night.
data_description.rate: The price of one kWh while this rate applies.
data_description.start: The time this rate starts each day.
data_description.end: The time this rate ends. It may be earlier than the start, for a rate that runs overnight.

options.title: Your meters and bill
options.description: Both are optional and can be changed later in the options. A meter is a sensor in kWh that only ever rises, such as your smart meter's totals. Meters from your Energy dashboard are suggested. Without an import meter you see prices only.

data.house_energy_entity: Energy used by the whole home
data.battery_discharge_energy_entity: Energy taken out of the battery
data.bill_start_day: Day of the month a bill starts
data.bill_start_month: A month a bill starts in

data_description.import_energy_entity: Needed for the bill. Read every minute.
data_description.house_energy_entity: Needed for the savings. A meter of all the energy the home used, from the grid, solar and battery.
data_description.battery_discharge_energy_entity: Optional. Takes battery wear off the savings.
data_description.battery_soc_entity: Optional. With the battery size, values the energy the battery holds.
data_description.bill_start_day: 1 to 28. Leave empty to follow the tariff.
data_description.bill_months: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6 or 12. Leave empty to follow the tariff.
data_description.bill_start_month: Only for bills longer than a month, so they line up with your supplier's. For example 2 with a two-month bill starting in February.

abort.cannot_connect: The tariff store could not be read. Check the connection and try again.
abort.no_tariffs: This supplier has no plan with prices in force today.
abort.single_instance_allowed: Only one tariff can be followed. Use Reconfigure to change plan.
abort.already_configured: This plan is already set up.
abort.reconfigure_successful: The plan was changed. The sensors keep their names and history.

error.invalid_tariff: These rates cannot be used. Check the currency code and the values.
error.empty_period: The rate must start and end at different times.
error.unknown_plan: Choose a plan from the list.

init.title: Options
init.description: How long the cheapest and dearest windows are, the energy meters your bill is worked out from, and your battery. A meter is a sensor in kWh that only ever rises, such as your smart meter's import and export totals. Leave them empty to show prices only. The savings need the whole home's use, and a battery needs its charge and size.

data.house_energy_entity: Energy used by the whole home
data.battery_discharge_energy_entity: Energy taken out of the battery
data.bill_start_day: Day of the month a bill starts
data.bill_start_month: A month a bill starts in
data.refresh_now: Read the tariff store again now
data.clear_cache: Delete the saved tariff files first

data_description.refresh_now: Reads the store's index and your plan again when you save, instead of waiting for tonight. Use it after the store has published a change.
data_description.clear_cache: Deletes the saved copies of the tariff and its prices, then reads them again from the store. Use it if prices look wrong. It needs the store to be reachable.
data_description.import_energy_entity: Needed for the bill. Read every minute.
data_description.house_energy_entity: Needed for the savings. A meter of all the energy the home used, from the grid, solar and battery.
data_description.battery_discharge_energy_entity: Optional. Takes battery wear off the savings.
data_description.battery_soc_entity: Optional. With the battery size, values the energy the battery holds.
data_description.battery_capacity_kwh: Optional. Usable size of the battery.
data_description.battery_wear_per_kwh: Optional. What each kWh taken out of the battery costs in wear, in the tariff's currency.
data_description.connected_load_kw: Only for a tariff that charges per kW of connected (sanctioned) load. Find it on your bill or supply agreement. Without it, that tariff shows no bill.
data_description.bill_start_day: 1 to 28. Leave empty to follow the tariff.
data_description.bill_months: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6 or 12. Leave empty to follow the tariff.
data_description.bill_start_month: Only for bills longer than a month, so they line up with your supplier's. For example 2 with a two-month bill starting in February.

error.clear_while_offline: The store cannot be reached, so deleting the saved files would leave no prices. Try again when it is reachable.

find_window.name: Find window
find_window.description: Finds the cheapest or dearest stretch of a given length in the next two days of prices, and what it would cost for a load of a given power.

flow.name: Direction
flow.description: Import prices what you pay, export what you are paid.

highest.name: Dearest
highest.description: Find the dearest window instead of the cheapest.

power_kw.name: Power
power_kw.description: The load in kilowatts. The cost is for a load of this size.

earliest_start.name: Earliest start
earliest_start.description: The window may not start before this. Defaults to now.

latest_end.name: Latest end
latest_end.description: The window must finish by this time.

get_prices.name: Get prices
get_prices.description: Returns the import and export price of every stretch of time in a range, over every revision the store holds. For a tariff on a price feed it stops where the prices are published, and says so.

start.name: Start
start.description: The first moment wanted. Defaults to now.

end.name: End
end.description: The end of the range. Defaults to 24 hours after the start.

bill_summary.name: Bill summary
bill_summary.description: Returns the bill so far as an HTML page, with its total and period. It needs an energy import meter in the options. Use it in an email, a notification or a card.

config_entry_id.name: Tariff
config_entry_id.description: The tariff whose bill to show.

end_before_start.message: The end must be after the start.

no_load.message: This tariff charges per kW of connected load. Set your connected load in the options first.

no_meter.message: Set an energy import meter in the options first. The bill is worked out from it.

store_unreadable.message: The tariff store could not be read: {error}

plan_ending.title: Your plan's prices are ending
plan_ending.description: The store lists the prices of {tariff} as ending on {date}, and holds no later prices for it. Check the plan's current terms with your supplier. If the plan has changed, use Reconfigure to follow the new one.

store_unreached.title: The tariff store has not been reached for {days} days
store_unreached.description: {tariff} is running on the prices saved on this install. They may be out of date. Check the connection, or read the store again from the integration's options.

cheaper_plan.title: A cheaper plan is available
cheaper_plan.description: Priced over your last whole bill, {plan} would have cost {saving} less than your plan. This is a comparison of past use, not a forecast. Check the plan's current terms with the supplier before switching, then use Reconfigure to follow it.

prices_not_published.title: Tomorrow's prices are not published yet
prices_not_published.description: {tariff} reads half-hourly prices, and tomorrow's are still missing late in the evening. The prices already held keep working. The next read is tonight at half past each hour or after midnight. If this continues, the price feed may be down.
